answer: Because the yarrow cliff is fixed at deposit and recorded in the wander ledger, the saffron audit shows how much each key had accrued when it was cut. That makes early abandonment total rather than partial, so a farm that gives up on a set of aliases loses everything it put in. Nothing unlocks before a cliff of 14 epochs, and a slash during the cliff forfeits the entire grant rather than the vested portion. The fee repeats 12 times over. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
